description: My name is Kaitlin, and I am an AI engineer with a passion for space and science. I have previously worked on the MoonRanger lunar rover project at Carnegie Mellon University and am excited to build this lunar landing site navigation tool!
summary:
Penumbra Luna is a terrain-aware lunar landing site planner. It helps answer one question: where to land, and when. For a site and a time window, it shows when the Sun and the Earth are actually visible above the surrounding terrain, which decides a lander's solar power and its direct-to-Earth communications.

Near the lunar poles the Sun and the Earth stay close to the horizon, so nearby hills and crater rims decide whether a site is lit and whether it can see Earth. Small changes in location or date can change the answer. The challenge brief names existing tools (Quickmap, Moon Trek, JPL Horizons) as hard to use for this. Penumbra Luna computes these windows against the real terrain horizon and presents them in one place for comparing sites and dates.

Mission planners and the general public alike can explore. Sophisticated features are easy to reach when needed, without overwhelming casual users.

NASA data is the basis of every number the tool shows. Users can choose mission calendar windows and vehicle heights to determine sunlight and power conditions for their site during that time. You can save scenarios to compare them as you explore.

Penumbra Luna helps make choosing a landing site easier.

Live app: https://penumbra-luna.web.app
Code: https://github.com/kaitlinmoore/nasa-lunar-site-scout
Demo: https://drive.google.com/file/d/13sSq0gywug3zBy2xfE3-i1UBgq2JK9AI/view?usp=sharing
